In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the current transport mechanism for the Al/(Bi 2S3-Polyvinyl Alcohol)/p-Si junction in the temperature range between 220 K and 380 K is a combination of the thermally activated tunneling (TAT) and the single GD of the BH for the L and M regions.
the current transport in the Al/(Bi 2S 3-PVA)/p-Si diode is controlled by the single Gaussian distribution of BH in both LBR and MBr.
the current transport mechanisms of this structure can be successfully interpreted by the GD of BH in both regions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Al/(Bi 2S3-Polyvinyl Alcohol)/p-Si diode has been fabricated and characterized by current-voltage measurements in the temperature range between 220 K and 380 K.
the current transport mechanism for the Al/(Bi 2S3-PV A)/p-Si junction is dominated by the single GD model for both the LBR and the MBR in the temperature range between 220 K and 380 K.
the current transport in the LBR and the MBR is due to the TE and the thermally-assisted tunneling (TAT), respectively.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, by using a PVA capping agent, it is possible to prepare bismuth sulfides with a high crystalline phase and the obtained Schottky diodes show a good electrical performance.
the PVA–Bi2S3 nanocomposite is an appropriate material for the fabrication of Schottky diodes.
the GD model is a more appropriate approach to describe the non-ideal I-V-T characteristics of the Al/(PBA-Bi2S2)/p-Si structures than the TE theory.
